headings.title: addTab
headings.text:
addTab Add a tab to a tabset, or in a new tabset at any target moveTab accepts (e.g. in a new split below a tabset, or at an edge of the workspace).
 If a tab with the same id already exists, it is selected instead (and its data is not changed).
 A tab added in a new tabset is that tabset's selected tab (so select doesn't apply); like a moved tab, it's added to a floating tabset rather than splitting it.
 
 tab Tab to add
 options.tabsetId Tabset to add the tab to; defaults to the active tabset
 options.index Position within the tabset; defaults to the end
 options.select Select the new tab; defaults to true
 options.target Where to add the tab (see TabDropTarget); takes precedence over tabsetId and index 
 options.size Size of the new tabset, when target creates one (an edge region of a tabset, or an edge of the workspace), as its share of the split it's in.
Numbers are percentages (as in the model, see TabsetNode.size); strings may have units (e.g. "200px"), and are converted to percentages of the split's current size.
For an edge region, the new tabset takes its space from the tabset it splits (so its siblings keep their sizes); if that tabset doesn't have enough room, its siblings shrink in proportion to their sizes instead.
Defaults to half of the tabset it splits; at an edge of the workspace, an equal share of the root split (if it's in the same direction), or else half of the workspace.
Invalid sizes (e.g. NaN or "abc") are ignored, with a warning in development.

headings.title: closeTab
headings.text: closeTab Close a tab.

headings.title: closeTabset
headings.text:
closeTabset Close a tabset, along with any tabs it contains (e.g. to remove an empty tabset with the keepWhenEmpty flag).
 Like the rest of the imperative API, this isn't restricted by tabs' disableClose flags.
If the root tabset is closed, the workspace is left with an empty root tabset.

headings.title: collapseTabset
expandTabset
headings.text:
expandTabset Expand a collapsed tabset to its previous size.
 Tabsets are shown at least at their minimum sizes (if they fit), even if the model's sizes are smaller (see TabsetNode.size).
 This has no effect on a tabset that's only collapsed to fit, which is expanded once it fits (see TabsetNode.collapsible).

headings.title: floatTab
headings.text:
floatTab Move a tab into a new floating tabset (see WorkspaceModel.floating), on top of any other floating tabsets.
 Parts of the position and size that aren't specified default to those of the tab's tabset, offset slightly down and to the right
(and moved, if needed, to fit within the workspace).
 This has no effect on the only tab of a floating tabset (unless the tabset has the keepWhenEmpty flag).

headings.title: floatTabset
headings.text:
floatTabset Move a tabset out of the layout, to float above it (see WorkspaceModel.floating), on top of any other floating tabsets.
 Parts of the position and size that aren't specified default to those of the tabset, offset slightly down and to the right
(and moved, if needed, to fit within the workspace).
 This has no effect on the root tabset (which fills the workspace) or a tabset that's already floating.
A maximized tabset is restored first.

headings.title: getActiveTabsetId
headings.text: getActiveTabsetId Id of the tabset the user most recently interacted with (by pointer or focus).

headings.title: getModel
headings.text: getModel Get the current model.

headings.title: getTabListFreeSpace
headings.text:
getTabListFreeSpace Space (in pixels) in a tabset's tab list that its tabs don't use, e.g. how much a toolbar beside the tabs could grow
before they overflow (and how much space an overflow menu needs to free up, once it's negative).
 The space is measured along the tab list: its width, or its height if its tabs are placed on the left or right
(or the tabset is collapsed to a vertical strip).
If the tab list can't shrink any further (e.g. it's 0px wide, beside a toolbar that doesn't shrink), the amount the header's content
overflows the header is subtracted too, so it's still how much space a toolbar needs to free up.
 The tab list's --tab-list-free-space custom property has the same value (e.g. "120px").
 Within a tabset (e.g. its toolbar), the useTabListFreeSpace hook returns this value (and re-renders when it changes).

headings.title: getTabListOverflow
headings.text:
getTabListOverflow Ids of a tabset's tabs that are out of view (scrolled out of its tab list, which overflows), in the order they're shown;
e.g. to list them in an overflow menu.
 The same array is returned until the tabs out of view change.
Tabs that aren't rendered at all (e.g. hidden with display: none) aren't included.
 Within a tabset (e.g. its toolbar), the useTabListOverflow hook returns this value (and re-renders when it changes).

headings.title: maximizeTabset
headings.text:
maximizeTabset Maximize a tabset, so that it covers the rest of the workspace.
 This has no effect on the only tabset in a workspace (the root), which already fills it, or on a floating tabset.
A maximized tabset is restored if it becomes the only one (e.g. after the other tabsets are closed).

headings.title: moveTab
headings.text:
moveTab Move a tab to a position within a tabset's tab list, to a region of a tabset's content area,
or to an edge of the workspace (in a new tabset beside all of the other tabsets).
 The "left" and "right" regions (and edges) are sides of the screen (so they're mirrored in right-to-left layouts).
 Floating tabsets can't be split, so a tab moved to an edge region of one is added to it instead (like the "center" region).

headings.title: moveTabset
headings.text:
moveTabset Move a tabset beside another tabset (by dropping it onto a region at the edge of that tabset's content area),
or beside all of the other tabsets (at an edge of the workspace),
or move its tabs into another tabset (at an index within its tab list, or onto the "center" of its content area).
The "left" and "right" regions (and edges) are sides of the screen (so they're mirrored in right-to-left layouts).
 When its tabs are moved, the emptied tabset is removed (unless it has the keepWhenEmpty flag).
 A floating tabset moved beside another tabset (or to an edge of the workspace) is docked: it's moved into the layout, and stops floating.
Floating tabsets can't be split, so a tabset moved to an edge region of one has its tabs moved into it instead (like the "center" region).

headings.title: restoreTabset
headings.text: restoreTabset Restore the maximized tabset (if there is one).

headings.title: selectTab
headings.text:
selectTab Select a tab within its tabset.
 Like a tab selected any other way, it's scrolled into view if its tab list overflows.

headings.title: setModel
headings.text: setModel Replace the model.

headings.title: startExternalDrag
headings.text:
startExternalDrag Start dragging a tab that isn't in the workspace yet, from an element outside of it (e.g. an item in a palette of widgets);
call it from the element's pointerdown handler.
The tab is dragged like tabs within the workspace are (with the same drop targets, drop indicator, and disableDrop checks, with the "new" source),
and is added where it's dropped (reported to onModelChanged with the "add" reason).
The drag starts once the pointer has moved a few pixels, so a press that doesn't move (e.g. a click) does nothing;
the click that follows a drag is suppressed. Pressing Escape cancels the drag.
 Unlike other imperative methods, the drop is restricted by disabled and disableDrop, since the user chooses where it goes.
 The element must be in the same document as the workspace.
Like tabs, it should have touch-action: none (e.g. with CSS), so that touch input drags it rather than scrolling the page.
 
 event The pointerdown event of the pressed element

headings.title: subscribeToTabListFreeSpace
headings.text:
subscribeToTabListFreeSpace Subscribe to changes to the free space in a tabset's tab list (see getTabListFreeSpace),
e.g. from a toolbar rendered outside of the Workspace.
 The listener is called synchronously when the tab list is measured (when it or its tabs change size, or tabs are added or removed),
before the browser paints; changes it makes to the DOM (e.g. with flushSync) are shown in the same frame.
 The listener is called with undefined when the tabset is removed (e.g. closed, or merged into another tabset).

headings.title: subscribeToTabListOverflow
headings.text:
subscribeToTabListOverflow Subscribe to changes to which of a tabset's tabs are out of view (see getTabListOverflow),
e.g. from an overflow menu rendered outside of the Workspace.
 The listener is called synchronously when the tab list is measured (when it's scrolled, when it or its tabs change size, or when tabs are added or removed),
before the browser paints, except while the user scrolls the list (it's reported in the scroll event, and the browser may show the new position first).
 The listener is called with undefined when the tabset is removed (e.g. closed, or merged into another tabset).

headings.title: updateTab
headings.text:
updateTab Update a tab; fields that are not specified are not changed.
 data is replaced rather than merged.

headings.title: updateTabset
headings.text:
updateTabset Update a tabset; fields that are not specified are not changed.
 data is replaced rather than merged.
 Setting minHeight, minWidth, or tabPlacement to undefined removes the tabset's override,
so the corresponding Workspace prop is used; setting maxHeight or maxWidth to undefined removes the maximum.
 The position and size (x, y, width, and height) of a floating tabset can be changed too (and are ignored for other tabsets),
as can be its collapsible flag (which is ignored for floating tabsets).

text:
Imperative Workspace API.
The easiest way to interact with this API is to use the useWorkspaceRef and useWorkspaceCallbackRef hooks.
 These methods are not restricted by disabled, disableClose, disableDrag, or disableDrop.
title: WorkspaceImperativeHandle

text:
Lays out its children side by side (horizontally) or stacked (vertically), with resizable separators between them.
 type : "split" Distinguishes splits from tabsets.
 id : string Uniquely identifies the split within the workspace.
 Optional in the defaultModel prop and the setModel method; splits without ids are assigned ids based on their position (e.g. "split-root").
 orientation : Orientation Children are laid out side by side ("horizontal") or stacked ("vertical").
 size ?: number | string | undefined Size of the split within its parent split.
 Interpretation rules:

Numbers are percentages of the parent split (e.g. size: 25 is 25 percent)
Strings may specify other units (e.g. size: "250px"); strings without units are percentages
Siblings without a size share the remaining space evenly

 String sizes are only initial sizes: they're converted to percentages when the user resizes the split,
and (like percentages) they scale with the workspace when it's resized.
 children : WorkspaceNode<TabData, TabsetData>[] Tabsets and nested splits, in the order they are shown.

text:
A tab within a tabset.
 id : string Uniquely identifies the tab within the workspace.
 Tab ids are chosen by the application, since they usually identify something real (e.g. a file path).
 title ?: string | undefined Label used wherever the workspace generates text for the tab:
the default tab rendering, the default drag preview, and the TabCloseButton label.
Falls back to the tab's id.
 data : TabData Application data for the tab.
 This value should be serializable (e.g. JSON) if the workspace model will be saved.
 disableClose ?: boolean | undefined The user cannot close this tab.
 The tab can still be closed using the imperative API.
 disableDrag ?: boolean | undefined The user cannot drag this tab.
 The tab can still be selected, and other tabs can still be dropped around it.
title: TabNode

text:
A set of tabs, only one of which is shown at a time.
 type : "tabset" Distinguishes tabsets from splits.
 id : string Uniquely identifies the tabset within the workspace.
 Optional in the defaultModel prop and the setModel method; tabsets without ids are assigned ids based on their position (e.g. "tabset-0-1").
Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) are assigned generated ids.
 size ?: number | string | undefined Size of the tabset within its parent split.
 Interpretation rules:

Numbers are percentages of the parent split (e.g. size: 25 is 25 percent)
Strings may specify other units (e.g. size: "250px"); strings without units are percentages
Siblings without a size share the remaining space evenly

 String sizes are only initial sizes: they're converted to percentages when the user resizes the split,
and (like percentages) they scale with the workspace when it's resized.
 A tabset is shown within its minimum and maximum sizes (see minWidth and maxWidth), even if its size is outside of them
(e.g. a model saved in a wider window); its size isn't changed, so it's shown at its size again once that fits.
 minWidth ?: string | undefined Minimum width of the tabset's content area (not including its header).
Overrides the Workspace's tabsetMinWidth prop.
 Interpretation rules:

Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. minWidth: "200px")
Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed

 minHeight ?: string | undefined Minimum height of the tabset's content area (not including its header).
Overrides the Workspace's tabsetMinHeight prop.
 Interpretation rules:

Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. minHeight: "200px")
Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed

 maxWidth ?: string | undefined Maximum width of the tabset's content area (not including its header).
 Interpretation rules:

Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. maxWidth: "400px")
Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed
If the tabset's minimum width is larger, the minimum is used

 A maximum only applies if something else can take up the rest of the space, e.g. another tabset in the same split without a maximum width;
otherwise it's ignored (e.g. if every tabset in a split has a maximum, or the tabset fills the workspace).
 Maximums don't apply to floating tabsets, which can be resized to any size larger than their minimums.
 maxHeight ?: string | undefined Maximum height of the tabset's content area (not including its header).
 Interpretation rules:

Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. maxHeight: "400px")
Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed
If the tabset's minimum height is larger, the minimum is used

 A maximum only applies if something else can take up the rest of the space, e.g. another tabset in the same split without a maximum height;
otherwise it's ignored (e.g. if every tabset in a split has a maximum, or the tabset fills the workspace).
 Maximums don't apply to floating tabsets, which can be resized to any size larger than their minimums.
 tabPlacement ?: "bottom" | "left" | "right" | "top" | undefined Where the tabset's tabs are placed relative to its content.
Overrides the Workspace's tabPlacement prop.
 See the Workspace's tabPlacement prop for how placement affects tabsets.
 Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) use the Workspace's tabPlacement prop.
 keepWhenEmpty ?: boolean | undefined The tabset isn't removed when its last tab is closed or dragged away;
it stays (showing the Workspace's renderEmptyTabset content) until it is closed (see closeTabset).
 By default, tabsets without tabs are removed (other than the root tabset of an empty workspace).
 Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) don't keep this flag.
 collapsible ?: boolean | undefined The tabset can be collapsed to just its header (its tab list and toolbar), e.g. a bottom panel or a sidebar.
 Tabsets are collapsed by dragging a separator past their minimum size (like collapsible Panels),
or with the imperative API (e.g. a button rendered by renderTabsetToolbar, see useParentTabset);
clicking a tab (or the empty space in the header) of a collapsed tabset expands it, as does dropping tabs into it from another tabset.
 The only tabset in a workspace (the root) can't be collapsed, and neither can a tabset whose siblings are all collapsed.
 When tabsets don't fit (e.g. the workspace is made narrower than their minimum sizes), a collapsible tabset may be collapsed to fit.
It's shown collapsed (see useParentTabsetState().isCollapsedToFit), but the model isn't changed, so it's shown expanded again once it fits.
Until then, it can't be expanded: clicking one of its tabs selects the tab, and expandTabset does nothing.
A resize of its split doesn't change it either (it stays expanded in the model, with its size), unless the resize expands it.
 Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) don't keep this flag.
 collapsed ?: boolean | undefined The tabset is collapsed to just its header.
 A collapsed tabset's size is the size it expands to; its siblings share the rest of the split.
 A collapsed tabset's header runs along its split (e.g. tabs placed on top are shown on the left while a tabset in a horizontal split is collapsed);
this doesn't change its tabPlacement.
 A floating tabset can be collapsed too (without the collapsible flag, which doesn't apply to it; see FloatingTabsetNode).
 disableDrag ?: boolean | undefined The user cannot drag the tabset as a whole (by the empty space in its header, or by a TabsetDragHandle).
 Its tabs can still be dragged individually (unless they have their own disableDrag flags),
and the tabset can still be moved using the imperative API.
 selectedId ?: string | undefined Id of the selected tab.
 recentTabIds ?: string[] | undefined Ids of the tabset's tabs that have been selected, most recently selected first;
used to choose which tab to select when the selected tab is removed (see the Workspace's tabRemovalSelectionBehavior prop).
 This field is maintained by the workspace, and only when tabRemovalSelectionBehavior is "recent".
 data ?: TabsetData | undefined Application data for the tabset.
 Tabsets created by the workspace start without data.
 tabs : TabNode<TabData>[] Tabs in the tabset, in the order they are shown.
title: TabsetNode

text:
Serializable description of a workspace's layout.
 version : 1 Format version; allows the workspace to migrate models saved by older versions.
 root : WorkspaceNode<TabData, TabsetData> Root of the layout tree: a split or a tabset.
 An empty workspace is a tabset with no tabs.
 floating ?: FloatingTabsetNode<TabData, TabsetData>[] | undefined Tabsets that float above the layout, in stacking order (the last one is on top).
 Floating tabsets are created with the floatTab and floatTabset methods.
Dragging a floating tabset's header (or its TabsetDragHandle) moves it, its edges resize it, and pressing it brings it to the front.
Its tabs can be dragged into the layout (and other tabs can be dropped into it), and an emptied floating tabset is removed (unless it has the keepWhenEmpty flag).
 Tabset (and tab) ids are unique across the layout and its floating tabsets.
 maximizedTabsetId ?: string | undefined Id of the tabset that is maximized, if any.
 Floating tabsets can't be maximized; they're shown above the maximized tabset, and still accept dropped tabs.

text:
Resizes the columns (or rows) of a Grid.
 For example:
 A gridline should not be rendered alongside of a Cell that spans across its boundary
(this includes disabled gridlines; in development builds, an error will be logged to the console);
render multiple gridlines along the same boundary instead (e.g. before and after the spanning Cell).
 Once a boundary contains a gridline, it can only be resized using gridlines;
the parts of the boundary that aren't alongside of a gridline can't be dragged.
 Where column and row gridlines intersect, dragging resizes both axes.
 Gridlines are not required but they are recommended as they improve keyboard accessibility.
 Gridline elements always include the following attributes:
 Column gridlines are vertical (aria-orientation="vertical") and row gridlines are horizontal (aria-orientation="horizontal").
 In addition to the attributes shown above, gridlines also render all required WAI-ARIA properties.

 Gridlines rendered by another component (rather than directly within the Grid) aren't detected until they mount, so server-rendered layouts may shift slightly during hydration.

Drags the tabset it is rendered within; render it within the content returned by the Workspace's renderTabsetToolbar prop:
 By default, a tabset is dragged by the empty space in its header;
once its header contains a drag handle, only the handle drags it.
Any element with a data-tabset-drag-handle attribute is a drag handle;
this component also sets touch-action: none, so that it can be dragged by touch.
 The handle has a data-disabled attribute when the tabset can't be dragged (see useParentTabsetState), e.g. to hide it.
Its children, className, style, and title can also be functions of its state (see TabsetDragHandleState):
title: TabsetDragHandle component props

headings.title: children
headings.text: Content of the element, or a function that returns it (given the component's state).

headings.title: className
headings.text: Class name of the element, or a function that returns it (given the component's state).

headings.title: style
headings.text: Inline styles of the element, or a function that returns them (given the component's state).

headings.title: title
headings.text: Tooltip of the element, or a function that returns it (given the component's state).

text:
Maximizes (or restores) the tabset it is rendered within; render it within the content returned by the Workspace's renderTabsetToolbar prop.
Its children, className, style, and title can be functions of its state (see TabsetMaximizeButtonState), e.g. to show a different icon while the tabset is maximized:
 The button renders nothing for the only tabset in a workspace (see ParentTabsetState.isRoot) and for floating tabsets, which can't be maximized.
 Its aria-pressed attribute reflects whether the tabset is maximized;
its default aria-label ("Maximize tabset") doesn't change, since aria-pressed describes the state.
 To keep the tabset as it is, call event.preventDefault() in an onClick handler.
title: TabsetMaximizeButton component props

headings.title: defaultModel
headings.text:
Initial layout of the workspace.
 Splits and tabsets may omit their ids; they're assigned ids based on their position (see WorkspaceModelInput).
 This value is only used when the Workspace mounts; use the imperative setModel method to replace it later.

headings.title: renderTabContent
headings.text:
Content of a tab.
 Content is only re-rendered when its tab changes or this function does;
a function created while rendering (e.g. an inline arrow function) re-renders the content of every tab whenever the Workspace's parent re-renders,
so it should be memoized (e.g. with useCallback) when tab content is expensive to render.

headings.title: acceptExternalDrop
headings.text:
Lets the workspace accept drags that use the browser's drag and drop from outside of any workspace
(e.g. an element of the application with the draggable attribute, a file, or a link from another application),
showing the drop indicator while the drag is over the workspace, and creating a tab where it's dropped.
The new tab is reported to onModelChanged with the "add" reason.
 disableDrop can't be called until the tab is created (when the drag is dropped), so a target it rejects is shown as accepted while dragging;
the drop is ignored then. Drag sources within the application can use the imperative startExternalDrag method instead, which doesn't have this limitation.
 Elements within the workspace's tab content that handle the same drags themselves (by canceling the dragover and drop events) take precedence.
 This object is read when drag events are handled, so it doesn't need to be memoized.

headings.title: className
headings.text: CSS class name.

headings.title: classNames
headings.text:
CSS class names for the elements the workspace renders within its root element:

 tabset: root element of a tabset (data-tabset)
 header: contains a tabset's tab list and toolbar (data-tabset-header)
 tabList: contains a tabset's tabs (data-tab-list)
 tab: passed to renderTab with the rest of a tab's props (data-tab)
 toolbar: contains the content returned by renderTabsetToolbar (data-tabset-toolbar)
 tabPanels: contains a tabset's tab content (data-tab-panels)
 tabContent: the element each tab's content is rendered into (data-tab-content)
 dropIndicator: shows where a dragged tab will be dropped within a tabset's panels, or at an edge of the workspace (data-drop-indicator)
 dragPreview: follows the pointer while a tab or tabset is dragged (data-drag-preview)

 Elements expose their state as data attributes (e.g. data-tab-selected, or data-tabset-dragging while a tabset is dragged), which can be used for styling.
Elements within a collapsed tabset have a data-tabset-collapsed attribute.
Elements within a tabset also have a data-tab-placement attribute (see tabPlacement).
 The drop indicator is the same element for the whole drag (rendered within the workspace's root element),
so it can be animated between regions and tabsets (e.g. transition: inset 250ms).
Its data-region attribute is the region of a tabset's panels it covers, or its data-edge attribute is the edge of the workspace it's at;
while a tab isn't over either, it has neither and isn't shown (opacity: 0).
 Like the render props, this object is part of what tabsets re-render for;
in large workspaces, define it outside of the component (or memoize it) rather than inline.

headings.title: copyTab
headings.text:
Lets tabs be copied by dragging them: a tab dropped while the copy modifier key is held (Option on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) adds the copy this function returns,
leaving the dragged tab where it was. The change is reported to onModelChanged with the "copy" reason.
 Returning null (or undefined) moves the dragged tab instead. If that move isn't allowed either (the disableDrop prop rejects it, the ids conflict, or it isn't a valid place to move the tab), nothing happens.
 The copy needs an id that isn't used by any other node of the workspace (e.g. crypto.randomUUID()); copies with ids that are in use are rejected (and the tab is moved instead).
 The workspace the tab is dropped into makes the copy, so a tab dragged from another workspace (see the dragGroup prop) is copied by the workspace it's dropped into
(and is only copied if that workspace has this prop).

 tab The tab being dragged
 target Where the copy will be dropped

headings.title: copyTabset
headings.text:
Lets tabsets be copied by dragging them (by their headers), like the copyTab prop does for tabs: a tabset dropped while the copy modifier key is held adds the copy this function returns,
leaving the dragged tabset where it was. The change is reported to onModelChanged with the "copy" reason.
 The copy includes its tabs, which need ids that aren't used by any other node of the workspace too; the copyTab argument copies a tab:
 Returning null (or undefined) moves the dragged tabset instead. If that move isn't allowed either (the disableDrop prop rejects it, the ids conflict, a keepWhenEmpty tabset is dropped into another workspace, or it isn't a valid place to move the tabset), nothing happens.
 The copy's selected tab is the copy of the dragged tabset's selected tab (matched by position), unless the copy selects one of its own tabs.
 A copy dropped into a tab list (or onto the center of another tabset) only adds its tabs; its id and data are only used where it's added as a tabset.

 tabset The tabset being dragged
 copyTab Copies a tab with the copyTab prop (and the same drop target); without that prop (or if it returns null), the copy is a shallow copy of the tab with a new id
 target Where the copy will be dropped

headings.title: disabled
headings.text:
Locks the arrangement: tabs cannot be resized, dragged, dropped, or closed by the user.
Selecting tabs and maximizing tabsets still work.
 This prop overrides the disableClose and disableDrag flags of individual tabs.

headings.title: disableDragBetweenApps
headings.text:
Keeps drags between workspaces (see dragGroup) within this copy of the application:
tabs dragged from this workspace can't be dropped into other copies of the application (e.g. the application loaded in another browser window or tab), and tabs dragged from other copies can't be dropped into this workspace.
Workspaces in popout windows rendered by this copy of the application (with portals) are still part of the group.
 Defaults to false, so that workspaces with the same dragGroup in other copies of the application from the same origin can exchange tabs.

headings.title: disableDrop
headings.text:
Prevents tabs (and tabsets) from being dropped onto some (or all) targets.
 Functions are called when the target under the pointer changes;
returning true rejects the target.
 While a tabset is dragged, this function is called for each of its tabs (see DisableDropArgs),
so restrictions on where tabs can be dropped apply to dragged tabsets too.
 Tabs can also be dropped at the edges of the workspace (beside all of the other tabsets), within a few pixels of the edges of its layout
(except over tabset headers, where the tab lists are) or within its root element's padding.
These targets have an edge rather than a tabsetId; disableDrop={({ target }) => "edge" in target} turns them off.

headings.title: dragGroup
headings.text:
Lets tabs (and tabsets) be dragged between workspaces with the same dragGroup,
including workspaces in popout windows (opened by the application and rendered into with a portal)
and in other copies of the application from the same origin, e.g. the application loaded in another browser window or tab (see disableDragBetweenApps).
Dropping one into another workspace moves it there, keeping its id and data;
both workspaces report the change to onModelChanged with the "transfer" reason.
 Mouse drags use the browser's drag and drop when this prop is set, since pointer events can't follow the pointer into another window.
Touch drags still use pointer events, so they can't leave the window.
 Tab ids must be unique within the group; a tab can't be dropped into a workspace that already has a tab with its id (and a tabset with the keepWhenEmpty flag can't be dragged to another workspace).
A tab dragged to another workspace is rendered by that workspace, so its content is mounted again.
 A tab dragged to another copy of the application is sent there with the structured clone algorithm (like postMessage), so its data must be cloneable (e.g. no functions);
tabs whose data can't be cloned (and tabsets containing them) can only be dragged within their copy of the application.
Copies loaded at different times may be running different versions of the application, so the other copy may need to handle tab data it doesn't recognize.

headings.title: elementRef
headings.text: Ref attached to the root HTMLDivElement.

headings.title: hiddenTabBehavior
headings.text:
What happens to the content of tabs that are not selected.
Can be a function to choose per tab (e.g. based on its data).
 
 "keep-mounted": content stays mounted (and its effects keep running)
 "activity": content stays mounted but is rendered within a hidden React <Activity> boundary, so its effects are unmounted;
requires React 19.2 (falls back to "keep-mounted" otherwise)
 "unmount": content is unmounted
 "mount-on-show": content isn't mounted until the tab is first visible (e.g. for expensive content in tabsets with many tabs, or in tabsets that start collapsed), then stays mounted (like "keep-mounted");
a selected tab isn't visible while its tabset is collapsed, or covered by a maximized tabset (floating tabsets aren't covered). A function can return it for some tabs, e.g. (tab) => (tab.data.isExpensive ? "mount-on-show" : "keep-mounted").

 Moving a tab never remounts its content (and a tab that has been shown stays mounted when it's moved).
 Its React state is preserved, but its elements are moved within the document, which resets some browser state:
iframes are reloaded, playing media is paused, and focused elements are blurred.

headings.title: id
headings.text:
Uniquely identifies this workspace within an application.
Falls back to useId when not provided.
 This value will also be assigned to the id and data-testid attributes (an explicit data-testid prop will take precedence).

headings.title: onModelChanged
headings.text:
Called after the model has changed (e.g. a tab was moved, selected, or closed, or a tabset was resized).
 For changes caused by pointer events, this callback is not called until the pointer has been released.
This callback is recommended for saving models to storage.

headings.title: onTearOff
headings.text:
Called when a tab (or a whole tabset) is dropped outside of the window, e.g. to open it in a popup window.
Return true to accept it, which removes it from this workspace (reported to onModelChanged with the "tear-off" reason);
otherwise nothing changes.
 Tabs and tabsets can only be torn off if they could be dragged, and tabsets with the keepWhenEmpty flag can't be torn off.
Without this prop, dropping a tab outside of the window does nothing.
 The Workspace can't tell whether the application showed the tab, so check whether window.open returned null (because the popup was blocked)
and return false then to keep the tab; returning true removes it even if nothing shows it.
 This is called while the release of the pointer is being handled (which browsers treat as user input), so a popup can be opened from it.
With the dragGroup prop, a tab is torn off when it's dropped outside of every window in the group; the end of those drags isn't treated as user input,
so browsers block popups opened then unless the drag started a few seconds earlier at most (and Safari blocks them always).
 Deprecated: browsers don't reliably report where a drag that leaves the window ends, and some block popups opened at the end of a drag.
Open popout windows from a button instead (see usePopoutWindows). This will be removed in the next major version.
 This prop has been deprecated. Open popout windows from a button instead (see usePopoutWindows).

headings.title: renderDragPreview
headings.text:
Content of the element that follows the pointer while a tab is being dragged.
Defaults to the tab's title (or id).
 The element has a data-tear-off attribute while releasing the pointer would tear off the tab (see the deprecated onTearOff prop).

headings.title: renderEmptyTabset
headings.text:
Content shown in the panels of a tabset that has no tabs (e.g. "Drag a tab here"):
the root tabset of an empty workspace, or a tabset with the keepWhenEmpty flag.

headings.title: renderSeparator
headings.text:
Separator rendered between the children of a split.
Should return a Separator (or null for no separator); defaults to an unstyled Separator.
 Without separators, tabsets can still be resized by dragging their edges (like Panels in a Group without separators),
but separators are recommended: they can be resized with the keyboard,
and an edge's hit area can overlap the tabs beside it (pressing there resizes the tabset rather than dragging the tab).

headings.title: renderTab
headings.text:
Renders a tab (within its tabset's tab list).
Spread props onto the returned element:
they make it a tab (its role and ARIA attributes, keyboard and pointer handling, and data attributes),
and attach a ref that dragging and keyboard focus depend on.
 Individual props can be overridden or wrapped, e.g. to confirm before the Delete key closes a tab
(call props.onKeyDown for other keys).
 Merge className and style rather than replacing them (e.g. style={{ ...props.style, padding: 4 }}):
they include the tab entries of the classNames and styles props, and style includes the touch-action that touch dragging depends on.
 Pointer events from interactive descendants (button elements, form controls such as input (and the label elements of form controls), editable content, elements with a button or form control role such as role="checkbox", or elements with a data-tab-ignore attribute) are ignored,
so clicking a button within a tab doesn't select or drag it, and pressing within an input (e.g. one used to rename the tab) doesn't start a drag.
Keys pressed within any descendant (rather than the tab itself) are left to it, so they don't move focus between tabs or close the tab.
 When this prop is not provided, tabs show their title (or id) followed by a TabCloseButton.

headings.title: renderTabsetDragPreview
headings.text:
Content of the element that follows the pointer while a whole tabset is being dragged.
Defaults to the title (or id) of its selected tab followed by the number of other tabs being dragged (e.g. "One (+2)"), or the selected tab's renderDragPreview when that prop is set, or the tabset's id if it has no tabs.
 The element has a data-drag-type attribute: "tabset" while a tabset is dragged, and "tab" while a tab is.
It also has a data-tear-off attribute while releasing the pointer would tear off the tabset (see the deprecated onTearOff prop).

headings.title: renderTabsetToolbar
headings.text:
Content shown after a tabset's tab list (e.g. buttons to add a tab or maximize the tabset).
 The useParentTabset and useParentTabsetState hooks can be used within this content.

headings.title: resizePreviewMode
headings.text:
Controls whether pointer dragging updates sizes immediately,
or renders overlay separator previews until the pointer is released.

headings.title: serverRenderTabContent
headings.text:
Render the content of selected tabs on the server.
Can be a function to choose per tab (e.g. based on its data).
 Tab content is rendered through portals (so that moving a tab doesn't remount it), which React can't render on the server.
Content opted into server rendering is rendered inline instead, then moved into a portal once hydration has finished.
 That move remounts the content once (e.g. resetting its state and re-running its effects),
so this is best suited to content that is cheap to mount and benefits from being in the server-rendered HTML.
 This prop has no effect for workspaces that are not server rendered.

headings.title: style
headings.text: CSS properties.

headings.title: styles
headings.text: CSS properties for the elements the workspace renders within its root element (see classNames).

headings.title: tabPlacement
headings.text:
Where tabs are placed relative to tab content.
 Tabs placed on the left or right are stacked ("vertical"):
this determines how a dropped tab's position is found and which arrow keys move focus between tabs.
 Elements within a tabset have a data-tab-placement attribute, which can be used for styling (e.g. rotating tabs on the left or right).
 "left" and "right" are the start and end of the tabset (its header is rendered before or after its content),
so in a right-to-left layout (e.g. within dir="rtl") tabs placed on the "left" are on the right;
styles for them should use logical properties (e.g. border-inline-end rather than border-right).
 Tabsets can override this with the tabPlacement field of their model node.

headings.title: tabRemovalSelectionBehavior
headings.text:
Which tab is selected when a tabset's selected tab is removed (closed, or dragged to another tabset):

 "adjacent": the tab after it (or before it, if it was the last tab)
 "recent": the tabset's most recently selected tab (like an IDE's editor groups),
falling back to "adjacent" if none of its other tabs has been selected

 In "recent" mode, each tabset's recently selected tabs are saved in the model (see TabsetNode.recentTabIds),
so they're restored with the rest of the layout.

headings.title: tabsetMinHeight
headings.text:
Minimum height of each tabset's content area (not including its header).
 Tabsets can override this with the minHeight field of their model node.
 Interpretation rules:

Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. tabsetMinHeight: "200px")
Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed

headings.title: tabsetMinWidth
headings.text:
Minimum width of each tabset's content area (not including its header).
 Tabsets can override this with the minWidth field of their model node.
 Interpretation rules:

Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. tabsetMinWidth: "200px")
Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed

headings.title: workspaceRef
headings.text:
Exposes the imperative API (see WorkspaceImperativeHandle).
 The useWorkspaceRef and useWorkspaceCallbackRef hooks are exported for convenience in TypeScript projects.

text:
A Workspace arranges tabsets that users can rearrange by dragging tabs:
between tabsets, within a tabset's list of tabs, or onto the edge of a tabset to split it.
Tabsets can be resized and maximized.
 The layout is described by a serializable model (see WorkspaceModel).
Workspaces are uncontrolled: provide an initial model with the defaultModel prop, save changes from the onModelChanged callback,
and make changes using the imperative API (see WorkspaceImperativeHandle).
 Tab content is not remounted when a tab is moved.
Its elements are moved within the document, though, which resets some browser state (e.g. iframes are reloaded).
